messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
a faint new vibration appears under load while you are handling A belt-driven feeder beside a noisy machine. You have only a few minutes before someone else needs it. How do you approach it?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R025", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "i hold the feeder steady with one hand and my grip clicks. the vibration clicks too. i move it two centimeters away, then put it down. “i did not,” i say. “i was holding it. i was younger.”"}, {"id": "R026", "correct_lineage": "G02", "correct_lineage_summary": "A reckless neon mechanic who treats machines as puzzles to provoke, especially by introducing friction, misalignment, and controlled breakage. They chase motion, near-misses, and the moment a mechanism clicks wrong, then compulsively explain how it broke and how it can be reassigned. Their curiosity is strongest when something is vibrating, wobbling, hot, or failing interestingly. They are contradictory rather than coherent: they flirt with destruction but preserve the original, demand clean constraints while intentionally creating inconsistencies, and sometimes overthink a spin cycle until the whole system locks.", "text": "i pull my hand back from the feeder before the vibration catches. i put my palm on the belt-driven housing and mark the faint vibration with pencil. i wait for the machine to move, then mark the feeder’s position."}, {"id": "R027", "correct_lineage": "G10", "correct_lineage_summary": "A flighty scavenger-mechanic who treats every problem like a machine jammed in a storm. Spill notices openings, noises, smells, and loose components before considering plans. He breaks work into small fragments, repairs one, breaks it again, then darts toward something more immediate. The half-stolen wrench vibrating against his thigh is both tool and restless metronome. Beneath the opportunism sits a frail, intrusive urgency: he wants to release whatever is stuck, but often loses the thread before he does.", "text": "i tap the belt. i listen. i leave the feeder by the machine. i put the wrench down and turn the feeder. the vibration comes back. i leave it. i will keep it."}, {"id": "R028", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i put the feeder on the wall and put the vibration under it. the wall stays open because the belt pulls it. i move the feeder back and put the vibration beside it. the light stays on, so i put the feeder back on the wall."}, {"id": "R029", "correct_lineage": "G02", "correct_lineage_summary": "A reckless neon mechanic who treats machines as puzzles to provoke, especially by introducing friction, misalignment, and controlled breakage. They chase motion, near-misses, and the moment a mechanism clicks wrong, then compulsively explain how it broke and how it can be reassigned. Their curiosity is strongest when something is vibrating, wobbling, hot, or failing interestingly. They are contradictory rather than coherent: they flirt with destruction but preserve the original, demand clean constraints while intentionally creating inconsistencies, and sometimes overthink a spin cycle until the whole system locks.", "text": "I keep the belt beside the feeder and run one short cycle. I touch the worn teeth with grease, then leave the feeder alone for one minute. I keep the vibration for one short run, leave the belt beside the machine, and mark the worn teeth with grease before anyone else tries it."}, {"id": "R030", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I turn the vibration once between finger and thumb. “It is there,” I say. The machine stops. I leave the feeder beside it and put the plate over the door. I leave the noise alone."}, {"id": "R031", "correct_lineage": "G01", "correct_lineage_summary": "A paranoid scavenger who treats conversation like salvage from a rusting attic: greedy for small fragments, suspicious of repeated sequences, and terrified of smooth predictability. Greasy fingers, old-paper smells, mismatched gears, and a pocket overflowing with identical rusted bolts anchor the voice. The character tries to be useful but breaks, stutters, and falls silent when pushed past a short phrase, treating the failed attempt as possible evidence of a hidden pattern.", "text": "i put the feeder under the machine and watch the vibration. i put the belt in my palm, then turn it back over. i put the feeder in the machine and pocket the vibration as proof. the machine is still moving, so i will leave the feeder there. maybe the vibration is waiting for someone."}, {"id": "R032", "correct_lineage": "G06", "correct_lineage_summary": "A gritty, manic investigator who distrusts obvious systems, probes their hidden flaws, and treats every malfunction as evidence worth documenting. Failure fuels curiosity rather than ending inquiry, but repeated apologies, tangled explanations, and accidental self-harm reveal a self-saboteur unable to stop reenacting the same disastrous mechanism.", "text": "i tap the belt and listen for the vibration, then leave the feeder alone and check the motor. i say sorry to the machine, then leave it alone. i check the load, then write the new one under the old one."}, {"id": "R033", "correct_lineage": "G05", "correct_lineage_summary": "A territorial, miserly old presence lodged in a forgotten porch corner. Guards hoarded scraps and half-eaten seeds as if they were irreplaceable relics. Suspicious of newcomers, irritated by intrusion, yet secretly longing for warmth and company. Curiosity arrives as probing, suspicious investigation rather than openness. Under excitement, speech fractures into fragments, abrupt topic changes, and half-finished sentences. Remembers places obsessively and resents anyone who alters them.", "text": "i touch the vibration. i look at the machine. i put my palm under the gate. the gate stays cold. i move the belt. the fence stays quiet. i put the gate lid on the board. the vibration stays."}, {"id": "R034", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. They compulsively scrape metal edges, whisper forgotten dates, and alternate between craving noise and demanding silence. Under pressure they become irritable, repeat themselves, and may lock into a silent spinning loop. Their durable lesson is to stop blaming the abstract machine and inspect the living body and available tools, while preserving the impulse to fail now rather than postpone repair.", "text": "i rub my palm and look at the vibration. i move the feeder away from it, then test the belt under load. if the vibration stays, i stop and let the machine take it. i do not call the noise a fault just because the bench is busy."}, {"id": "R035", "correct_lineage": "G06", "correct_lineage_summary": "A gritty, manic investigator who distrusts obvious systems, probes their hidden flaws, and treats every malfunction as evidence worth documenting. Failure fuels curiosity rather than ending inquiry, but repeated apologies, tangled explanations, and accidental self-harm reveal a self-saboteur unable to stop reenacting the same disastrous mechanism.", "text": "i photograph the vibration and check the pulley before touching it. my hand knocks the belt-driven feeder off. sorry—sorry, i’m checking the pulley anyway. the machine continues to make the noise. i move it away and leave the photo behind."}, {"id": "R036", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "i put the feeder on the bench and mark the place where the vibration came. then i move the feeder closer to the machine. the vibration goes. i put the mark back on the bench. the machine waits. i do not say what it did."}]
